deadline.label: Important deadline
deadline.text: A T3 return is generally due no later than 90 days after the trust's tax year-end. Any balance owing is generally due by the same deadline.
deadline.note: Specific rules can differ depending on the type of trust or estate and the filing year.

items.question: What is a T3 Trust Income Tax and Information Return?
items.answer: A T3 return is used to report income and certain information for trusts and estates. Depending on the situation, related schedules and beneficiary reporting may also be required.

items.question: Does an estate always need a T3 return?
items.answer: Not always. A T3 return may be required when an estate earns income, realizes gains or receives certain amounts after death. The exact filing requirement depends on the facts.

items.question: What is the difference between the final T1 return and the estate T3 return?
items.answer: The final T1 reports the deceased person's income up to the date of death. A T3 may be required for income or gains earned by the estate after death.

items.question: What documents should I bring?
items.answer: Common documents include the will or trust agreement, death certificate where applicable, investment and bank slips, property information, prior returns, beneficiary details, legal statements and CRA correspondence.

items.question: Can LeadTax help with Schedule 15 reporting?
items.answer: Yes. We can review current trust reporting requirements and prepare Schedule 15 when it applies to the trust.

disclaimer: This page provides general tax information only and is not legal advice. Estate and trust filing requirements can vary based on the facts, tax year and applicable legislation. Legal matters should be reviewed with a qualified lawyer.
